steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Conservative Party: centre-right, supports free market capitalism, low taxes, private enterprise, traditional values, and strong defence. Traditionally supported by business owners, middle-class and older voters. Key policies: lower taxation, privatisation, strong law and order.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Labour Party: centre-left, supports social justice, public services, workers' rights, and redistribution of wealth through taxation. Traditionally supported by working-class voters, trade unions and ethnic minorities. Key policies: NHS investment, higher minimum wage, nationalisation of key services.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Other parties: Liberal Democrats (centre, proportional representation, civil liberties, EU membership), Green Party (environmentalism, social justice, renewable energy), Reform UK (right-wing populist, Eurosceptic, lower immigration, lower tax), Scottish National Party (Scottish independence, centre-left social democracy), Plaid Cymru (Welsh interests).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: How government is formed: after a general election, the leader of the party with the most MPs usually becomes Prime Minister. If no party has a majority (hung parliament), parties negotiate to form a coalition (Conservative-Lib Dem 2010-2015) or a minority government with confidence-and-supply agreements. The PM appoints the Cabinet (about 20 senior ministers who run government departments).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Conservative = free market, low tax. Labour = social justice, public services. Key left-right divide in UK politics. Government formation: largest party -> PM -> appoints Cabinet. Hung parliament = coalition or minority government. PM power: SIGNIFICANT but CONSTRAINED by party, Parliament, media, public opinion. Not a president.
